nodes.label: Spotify client
nodes.summary: Plays audio, prefetches the next track, keeps an encrypted local cache of partial tracks (up to 10% of free disk, 50 MB–10 GB in 2010) and reports a stream after 30 seconds of playback.
nodes.details: Random access (user picks a track) is ~39% of playbacks. On a cache miss the 2010 client asked the server for ~15 seconds of audio over its open TCP connection.

nodes.label: Stateless API tier
nodes.summary: Authenticates the user, serves catalog and playlist metadata, and returns signed URLs for audio files. Horizontally scalable behind a load balancer.

nodes.label: Catalog / user DB (SQL)
nodes.summary: Tracks, albums, playlists and users. Read-mostly, so replicas absorb the load.

nodes.label: CDN
nodes.summary: Serves audio files near the listener using signed URLs and HTTP range requests.

nodes.label: Audio blob storage
nodes.summary: Encoded audio at several quality tiers. Audio dominates storage and egress, while metadata is tiny.
nodes.details: Current app tiers (Spotify Support): Low ≈24, Normal ≈96, High ≈160, Very high ≈320 kbit/s, Lossless up to 24-bit/44.1 kHz FLAC. Web player AAC 128/256 kbit/s.

nodes.label: Peer network (2010)
nodes.summary: In 2010, clients also served cached chunks to each other. Only 8.8% of played music data came from Spotify's servers. Spotify later removed P2P from the desktop client, and mobile and web never used it.
nodes.details: Peers do no re-encoding: a peer holding the q9 (≈320 kbps) version cannot serve a q5 (≈160 kbps) request.

nodes.label: Artist / label upload
nodes.summary: Uploads masters through a pre-signed URL (standard design).

nodes.label: Transcode + loudness measure
nodes.summary: Asynchronously encodes the quality tiers and measures loudness. The gain is applied at playback toward -14 dB LUFS (ITU 1770), and the audio files are left untouched.
nodes.details: The loudness behaviour is from Spotify Support. The async transcoding pipeline is the standard design.

nodes.label: Search index
nodes.summary: Updated from the catalog after publishing, so new tracks become searchable.

steps.caption: The client sends an authenticated request for a track. The API tier is stateless.
Metadata comes from the read-mostly catalog database.
The API returns a time-limited signed URL, so audio bytes never pass through the API.
The client fetches the audio with HTTP range requests, so it can seek and prefetch.
Only CDN misses reach blob storage. Streams are counted after 30 seconds of playback.

While asking the server for the first ~15 seconds, the client also searched the peer network for the rest of the track. By the paper's measurements only 8.8% of played data came from servers, and the median start latency was 265 ms.
Today's clients stream from servers and CDNs instead. Spotify removed P2P from desktop, and mobile and web never used it.
The artist's master goes straight to blob storage via a pre-signed URL.
An object-created event starts transcoding and loudness measurement.
Quality tiers are written back. Loudness is measured now, but the gain is applied at playback (-14 LUFS target).
The track is published to the catalog.
The search index is updated shortly after.
